LESSON: INTRODUCTION TO ELECTRONICS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: PHYSICS FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Electricity and Magnetism
Topic 3.3: Introduction to electronics
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Introduction to electronics, part of Electricity and Magnetism in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 PHYSICS FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How does temperature affect the resistance of conductors and semiconductor s? 2. Why are semiconductor s important in our day-to-day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Introduction to electronics together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: the learners demonstrate the skill of explanation as they analyze complex

problems by using logical reasoning, creating and testing hypothesis as they perform an experiment to investigate the

electrical behavior of conductors, semiconductors and insulators with varying temperatures.

• Digital literacy: the learner interacts with digital technology as they dismantle and assemble parts of digital devices

while performing an experiment to investigate the electrical behavior of conductors, semiconductors, and insulators

with varying temperatures.

Values:
• Social Justice: the learner demonstrates equity by according equal opportunities to each other when sharing

responsibilities while searching for information on applications of conductors, semiconductors, insulators and

superconductors from relevant sources and resources

• Unity: the learner ensures inclusion by collaborating with others as the learner works in a group to perform an

experiment to investigate the electrical behavior of conductors, semiconductors and insulators.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Citizenship: the learner acquires good governance skills by applying integrity and principles of leadership as they work

together to search for information on applications of conductors, semiconductors, insulators and superconductors from

relevant sources and resources.

Suggested learning resources;

Metals like; copper, aluminum and silver, aqueous solution of salt, plastics. rubber, paper, glass, digital devices, braille,

print materials’ silicon, lead telluride, sulfur, germanium, learners course book in print and braille,

Suggested key skill;

Investigate the electrical behavior of conductors, semiconductors and insulators with varying temperatures
